_comment: What this plugin needs the city research to gather. Any plugin may ship a research.json; generate.py collects them all and appends the asks to the niche research prompt. Declaring it here rather than in generate.py is the point — the plugin is the whole unit, and a site that does not have this plugin does not pay for the question.
_no_direction: We asked for a compass direction once and cut it. The data did not support it — 4 of 8 towns around Lufkin came back wrong, Pollok as 'S' when it is NW, off by 132 degrees — and more to the point the diagram did not need it: it was already unique per city, and a reader from Diboll is looking for the word 'Diboll', not for where its dot sits. Do not re-add it.
_neighborhoods_note: The base research prompt already ASKS for neighborhoods, so this entry has no ask of its own — it exists to set min_items. Without it a city that returned two names kept two forever: two is not empty, so the top-up never re-asked. Mold-site had 2 for Lufkin while water-site had 6, same city.

fields.ask: "nearby_towns" — an array of 4-8 SEPARATE towns or cities near {city}, {SS} that a local service business would realistically also cover. These must NOT be neighborhoods or districts of {city} itself — those belong in "neighborhoods". Each entry is an object with "name" (the town) and "miles" (approximate DRIVING distance from {city} as a plain number). Example: {"name": "Diboll", "miles": 10}. Only real, separately-named places you are confident exist; never invent one, and never list {city} itself. If you are confident of the town but not the distance, omit the "miles" key rather than guessing.
